cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Co-Sign This
cards.instruction: Get someone to help by making them an official participant who shares responsibility for the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've made you co-organizer of Saturday's school trip. Can you approve the bus route? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only volunteered to drive. Your route misses the museum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Good catch. Correct it and initial it; then we both own the plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fix it, but you explain any delays to the parents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together. I'll introduce you as our transport lead and take the questions beside you.

mechanism: A gives a reluctant volunteer formal transport responsibility while accepting route correction and taking the delay explanation burden.
confusable: Unlike simply assigning driving, A seeks initials and a named public role that keep B accountable for the route.
comparison: School-trip planning and parent questions differ from shared barbecue custody and replacement.
seedUse: D169-b museum omission, initials and transport lead; S02-b accepts B correction and requested split of parent questions.
